name: Constructivist Agitprop
summary: 1920s agitprop poster grammar: a teal wedge pierces the circle of blind spots and a megaphone shouts the anomaly.
look: Cream paper, ink and coral with teal as the heroic colour; everything on hard diagonals. Uppercase Manrope 800 slogans, mono captions riding on ink bands, geometric shards on impact.

components.name: Wedge
components.role: teal triangle that pierces the circle — Pulse cutting through blind spots

components.name: Diagonal bands
components.role: ink/coral/teal bars at −27°…+4° that carry mono captions

components.name: Megaphone cone
components.role: coral trapezoid emanating from the Acme mark; the anomaly is shouted in it

components.name: Shards
components.role: small rectangles scattered on impact frames

components.name: Slogan button
components.role: rotated block CTA with a ▶ glyph

motion.name: Slash-in
motion.how: bands translate along their own angle from off-frame, expo.out 0.35 s, landing on 8th-note offbeats

motion.name: Wedge strike
motion.how: wedge x from +700 px to 0, power4.in 0.25 s, impact exactly on the drop; 2-frame camera shake ±6 px

motion.name: Megaphone unfold
motion.how: cone scaleX 0→1 from its narrow end, back.out(1.4) 0.5 s = one beat, text scales 1.15→1 on the next downbeat

story: Hook: diagonal slogan "HOW MANY DASHBOARDS DID YOU CHECK TODAY?" with 38 in an ink circle and a coral band. Reveal: the teal wedge pierces the cream circle, ACME PULSE slams in. Proof: a megaphone from the Acme mark shouts "−18% checkout conversion", ink bands carry "since 09:42 · after deploy #2231", a human hits the ROLL BACK slogan block. CTA: "You ship. Pulse watches." with a START FREE band.
adapt: Make the wedge your product and the circle the problem it breaks; put your key alert or feature result inside the megaphone. Your CTA becomes the slogan on the final band.

references.note: El Lissitzky, 1919: the wedge piercing the circle
Rodchenko: diagonals, photomontage, the 1924 Lengiz 'Books' megaphone poster

fit.risk: Political connotations and aggressive tone; rotated type reduces readability if held too briefly.
